errors.english: In a ritual of motion with four actions
errors.why: gsol ba dang bzhi'i las is the jñapticaturtha-karman, a motion followed by three proclamations (the motion being the fourth), not a motion 'with four actions'; likewise gsol ba dang gnyis is motion plus one proclamation.

note: Sound rendering of a difficult Vinaya-sūtra commentary passage on when a formal act counts as done; terminology slightly loose.

errors.english: even if the object of sound is not diverse in nature
errors.why: sgra here is śabda 'word': conjunction (ldan pa), the referent of the word 'variegated', is not itself variegated in nature; 'object of sound' makes no sense.

fix.find: even if the object of sound is not diverse in nature
fix.replace: even if conjunction, the referent of the word, is not diverse in nature

errors.english: because of the (inherence) samavāya of many things in a single object of conjunction in a painting
errors.why: The Tibetan is ekārthasamavāya: conjunction inheres in one and the same substrate (as the colours), not 'inherence of many things in a single object of conjunction'.

note: Follows the anti-Vaiśeṣika argument on variegated cognition reasonably, but misreads 'word' as 'sound' and garbles the ekārthasamavāya point.

errors.english: when the pillars do not support [the load]
errors.why: gdung ma 'degs pa is 'lifting a beam' (gdung ma = beam); the example is of bearers individually unable, jointly able to lift the beam; no negation.

fix.find: when the pillars do not support [the load]

note: Generally faithful pratīka-commentary on the avayavin debate; one misread example.
Faithful rendering of the sūtra quotation on the Tathāgata's knowledge of causes of affliction and purification and of his absorptions.

errors.english: That itself is not a species.
errors.why: The root verse says they are not knowers of reality (tattvavid), as the commentary's 'only the Buddha knows reality' shows; rigs here is not 'species'.

fix.find: That itself is not a species.
fix.replace: They are not knowers of reality.

errors.english: Like a purposed person, or is it not even this?
errors.why: The argument is: the utterly non-existent would be born and die like the person you accept, or else this one too would not, since there is no difference; the English garbles the dilemma.

errors.english: error without a seed will not occur even in those who appear perversely
errors.why: 'Having inverted appearance' qualifies the error itself (a seedless error with distorted appearance would not occur), not persons.

note: The overall sense of the passage on non-Buddhas being corrupted by grasped/grasper comes through, but the root verse is mistranslated and the opening dilemma is garbled.

errors.english: Qualities are those conditioned things whose characteristics, such as impermanence, are distinguished
errors.why: Qualities are the attributes (impermanence etc., characteristics of those conditioned things) that are attached to them, not the conditioned things themselves.

errors.english: it is established as perceived because it is not obstructed
errors.why: bskal ba is viprakṛṣṭa, 'remote/inaccessible' (by place, time or nature, as the note itself says), not 'obstructed'; rendered so throughout.

note: Readable account of perception/non-perception and substance/quality; some referent and terminology slippage.

errors.english: cold and the like [act upon] fire and the like
errors.why: The example is fire etc. as the cause of diminution of cold etc. (cf. 'fire, which opposes cold' below), not cold acting on fire.

fix.find: cold and the like [act upon] fire and the like
fix.replace: fire and the like [act upon] cold and the like

note: Good rendering of the argument on the two kinds of destruction and on contradiction; one inverted example.

errors.english: let alone for many such teachings
errors.why: The Tibetan says one should give up bodies for Ganges-sand eons for each such teaching, let alone a single [body/life]; 'many teachings' is not in the text.

errors.english: what need is there for gold, jewels, pearls, or lapis lazuli to honor
errors.why: The merchant's daughter is offering (take) the gold, jewels etc. with which to honour Dharmodgata, not saying there is no need for them.

note: Sadāprarudita excerpt mostly correct, but the daughter's offer is turned into a rhetorical dismissal.

errors.english: Is born as a jewel among men, a blissful being
errors.why: bde bar 'gro ba is Sugata (Skt. prakaṭitasugataḥ): a jewel of a man who manifests the Sugata is born, not 'a blissful being'.

note: Colophon and opening verses of the Śāketa story rendered acceptably.

errors.english: When it arises in men who wish for harm
errors.why: Anger arises in oneself, and those who wish one ill rejoice when it does; it does not arise in the ill-wishers.

fix.find: When it arises in men who wish for harm
fix.replace: When it arises, the men who wish one harm

errors.english: Even though I was shaken, I did not let go.
errors.why: It is the harmer (anger) that was stirring which he did not release, not he who was shaken; the king's question repeats the same misreading.

errors.english: When it is born, one becomes unmanifest
errors.why: When anger arises one does not see [the good], as the next line (when unarisen, the good is seen) shows; 'one becomes unmanifest' and its note are wrong.

errors.english: If the anger that torments the heart is not present
errors.why: The verse contrasts with the next: one who does not give up heart-burning anger gains ill fame like the waning moon; the 'false accusation' reading and note invert it.

note: Jātakamālā verses on anger are readable, but several verses misassign who is angry or invert the point.
